sources.scope: Cited taxonomic article; item-level reuse rights remain unknown.

claims.text: The treatment's comparative diagnosis describes mature male Hyphessobrycon loweae with an elongated, filamentous dorsal fin. Compared with H. peugeoti, the examined H. loweae material is reported with six to seven horizontal scale rows from dorsal-fin origin to lateral line and 17-21 branched anal-fin rays (mode 20), versus five rows and 21-24 rays (mode 22) for H. peugeoti. These are treatment-level diagnostic comparisons, not estimates of all populations.

claims.placeTimeScope: Comparative diagnosis and meristic description in the 2013 treatment, pp. 38-40, Plazi rows 10-11. The fin character is explicitly restricted to mature males; the counts describe examined taxonomic material and do not quantify all populations.

claims.text: The authors report clear, slow-flowing streams with abundant submerged vegetation at named H. loweae localities, including Córrego Xavante, upper rio das Mortes, and rio Culuene tributaries near Gaúcha do Norte. They also cite paratypes from the small, densely vegetated Lago do Leo. These are locality-specific reports, not a complete or uniform habitat rule for the species.

claims.text: The authors report specimens collected in shallow areas under one metre deep in the early dry season, but the recorded sites differ: the type locality was a swampy, deforested roadside area beside preserved forest; MNRJ 29609 came from below a recently breached dam; the single MNRJ 29503 specimen came from a clear, sandy-bottom flowing stream with sparse aquatic vegetation; and named paratypes came from a flooded area beside the rio Juruena. These collection settings do not define a uniform species-wide niche.
